title: Film Kit
question: How does Film Kit rebuild a film's two editions from its tracked sources, and what holds each step to its inputs?
summary: Film Kit narrates each edition thought by thought with a pinned local voice model, assembles one soundtrack at one program level, times the captions, gates and renders the picture, and packages four films, a UHD master and a 1080p film each with captions and without. Each step records the SHA-256 of what it read, and a later step refuses a record bound to other bytes.
scope: The Film Kit engine as released at v0.24.1: the src/filmkit package, with its Python modules, Node tools and watch list, and the pyproject.toml and VERSION that package it.
limits: Each component cites every file the rules attribute to it; a relation cites the modules that make its call or run its process.

Relations are calls and process calls in the source, not runtime order, and not every call is drawn: reads of the film record and the spoken units, which most modules make, the calls that verification and review make across the build, the take judgment's calls into alignment and selection, and auditions' runs of the narration command are named in component details.
Tests, the sample film, the OpenSpec specifications and Changes, the documentation and the repository's tooling and CI are outside the scope.

exclude.reason: The engine's Python and Node tests.
The sample film that the tests load and the local acceptance builds; its text is written for the tests and is no film's source.
The engine's OpenSpec specifications and archived Changes: its accepted requirements and change history.
The README, the agent entry, the contributing guide and the change log; the guide cites them at the same revision.
The copyright notice and the licences of the sample film's assets and of the software and models a build installs.
The development lock; a film locks filmkit and its dependencies in its own project.
The npm packages that the tests and the sample film use; a film declares its own.
The lock of those npm packages.
Tool configuration: the Mise tasks and lock, linters, formatters and the CI projection.
The repository's ETHOS binding and release peers.
The proof sets that ETHOS and hosted CI run for this repository.

blocks.title: Before anything is narrated
items: Concepts
each segment says its declared concepts in approved words; no counterexample appears anywhere
Readings
each watched Chinese character has a declared reading, and every name a spoken form
Spoken text
one pronunciation contract per script derives what each thought says
Refusal
narration stops before any speech model loads, and names every failure

blocks.title: Before the picture renders
items: Frame audit
every frame at 1/30 s: layout, legibility, balance and how text lines up
Sync audit
each label against its spoken words; marks that wait for a name
Text measures
the declared title for 1 s before the first word; each text at rest at 4.5:1 or more
Motion audit
ghosts, stalls, pops, jumps and dash snaps at 30 frames per second
Detail audit
single lines, strokes and names, through every frame at 60 frames per second
Gate record
binds the composition, timeline, stylesheet, fonts and engine version

blocks.title: A take reaches the soundtrack only if it ends whole

details.edits: thoughts in place, moving each retake with its text

details.judges: a take of one thought by every line the film holds for a take: its length, ending, phrase ends, opening, unmarked pauses, declared terms, units and clarity, and names every failing line at once
details.holds: a take to its words: no unit of its transcript may differ from its text by reading
details.chooses: among the takes no line refuses, the one with the widest margin, then the quietest ending, then the lowest seed
details.asks: the selection's gates about each segment as they will measure it, where the narration's alignment stands beside the receipt; it transcribes each take with the pinned recognizer

details.aligns: each recording to its exact text with the pinned forced aligner
details.transcribes: each recording as a recognition proxy, not certification, and caches each transcript under its waveform, the language and the recognizer's identity
details.selects: the recordings and alignment bound to the current script and cast, within the film's pause limits and declared terms

details.installs: the pinned browser build and three speech models, each checked against its digests
details.network: the only step that reaches it

details.names: the spoken units, punctuation roles, joins and thought spans that sound, captions and audits share
details.measures: the heard pause at each word boundary, which selection and assembly limit, and the steps between thoughts, for listening

details.assembles: the selected takes with designed pauses at one program level
details.refuses: a take that ends abruptly without a declared release, an unmarked pause above its limit, and a declared term said unlike its reference
details.writes: the soundtrack, the timeline, the assembly receipt and the sound gate's record
details.judges: the assembled soundtrack by the review's measures, and refuses a segment under the film's clarity floor, an abrupt or cut ending and a stopped phrase
details.levels: on the tolerances a script declares, each thought within its segment, each segment within its chapter and each chapter within the film, each by one static gain

details.times: one-line cues on the exact aligned words, never across a thought
details.typesets: each cue's text, with typographic quotation marks; the narration and aligned words stay as written
details.writes: SRT, VTT, the transcript, the chapters and their metadata

details.audits: every frame at 1/30 s, each label's sync with its words, the opening title and each text's contrast, motion at 30 fps, and single lines, strokes and names at 60 fps
details.keeps: a finding of the detail audit or a run far off centre that the film declares as an exception, recorded with its reason
details.binds: composition, timeline, stylesheet, fonts and engine version in the gate record

details.runs: the engine's Node tools with the film's npm packages, from a copy in the film's tool cache
details.measures: text by the advance widths of the film's declared faces

details.runs: the film's composition headlessly on a canvas stand-in
details.measures: layout, legibility, balance, typography, the label and text traces, motion, and the detail of single lines, strokes and names
details.compares: each uncaptioned frame's paints with the captioned frame's, less its caption paints
details.proves: that the rows a derived uncaptioned picture paints hold caption paints and nothing else

details.checks: the staged picture's geometry and the delivered players in Chrome Headless Shell
details.paints: each edition's cover from the staged picture
details.draws: each whole turn the frame audit found, to find the arcs the browser paints without ink
details.names: the browser its checks run: the build the supply installs, or the one FILM_CHROMIUM_PATH names
details.takes: the picture's size, seconds and rate from the stage's record, and refuses a stage whose page states another size or length

details.stages: the picture's data, the composition's script and style, the fonts and one document that inlines them, bound in stage.json with the faces and the language
details.reads: every @font-face rule of the film's stylesheet once, for the audits' text table and the renderer, and refuses by name a rule it cannot hold the canvas to
details.renders: the captioned picture, and the uncaptioned one where it is not derived, with the native renderer only after a passing gate record
details.derives: the uncaptioned picture from the captioned one, for a film that declares software capture and a captioned picture the pinned canvas build drew, by one x264 encode that paints the caption band's rows in the ground
details.validates: each rendered picture's receipt, which must name the engine's canvas package, version and text renderer, its frames, size and cadence, and a keyframe every 2 s; a derived picture against its derivation's receipt
details.qualifies: the renderer by a second render of the captioned stage in another count of spans: the two must state one digest of their drawn frames and compare with no row left out
details.scans: a rendered film for speech over a still picture
details.compares: each edition's two pictures before packaging: a rendered pair at every frame, which may differ only by its captions and must keep its edge slivers within the bound; a derived pair by the derivation's receipt, decoding no picture

details.encodes: each frame through x264 with a keyframe every 2 s and no B-frames; a picture in four spans of whole groups of frames, one process each, joined by stream copy, and a draft in one process
details.pins: @napi-rs/canvas 1.1.1 and, for Apple silicon, the SHA-256 of its native library; a film that installs another version is refused

details.packages: four films, a UHD master and a 1080p film each with captions and without, with cover, release tags and chapters; each 1080p film encoded by x264 in software and keyed every 2 s, and no film with B-frames

details.names: the film's version from its VERSION, in each film and on both pages

details.refuses: a caption cue whose text is not typeset
details.writes: only each edition's duration record of the run, and nothing with --read-only; it reads and decodes

details.compares: a rebuild with the published release: bytes, decoded audio, container, and each frame's PSNR

details.delivers: the 25 delivery members to the film's delivery folder, then reads them back
details.destination: the folder --destination names, else the film's declared delivery_folder below the root FILMKIT_DELIVERY_ROOT names, else that name below the user's videos folder

details.serves: local review media with byte ranges
details.reads: the entry page and both players back in a real browser before rsync changes anything

details.prepares: an independent review round: set-aside, player binding, prompts and records
details.measures: rate, pauses, endings, levels, voice clarity, recognition and the picture records
details.reads: a segment's voice clarity over the whole soundtrack's kept frames whose centres lie in it, as the reviewers do
details.judges: each thought's ending by the criterion the assembly uses

views.title: From a film's sources to its delivered films
views.question: Which commands carry one edition from its script to its four delivered films?
views.summary: The narration command runs synthesis for the thought takes. The production command assembles the soundtrack, refreshes captions, checks the picture, renders it only after a passing gate record and packages four films. Both commands write a duration record when they end.

views.title: What the engine reads from a film
views.question: What does the engine read from the film it builds, and what must hold before narration?
views.summary: Film and editions reads the film repository's declaration and checks it before any work. The narration command first runs the word checks on concepts, readings and terms, and refuses before any speech model loads.

views.title: Narration and its supply
views.question: How is each thought narrated, auditioned and aligned, and what does the supply install first?
views.summary: Thought takes narrate each thought from the cast's seed or retake, and auditions try other seeds; the take judgment judges each take by the film's lines, and alignment and selection aligns each recording to its text. Supply installs the browser build and three speech models. No narration process outlives a narration that is asked to end.

views.title: One assembly for sound and captions
views.question: How do the selected takes become one soundtrack, a timeline and its captions?
views.summary: Soundtrack assembly sets the selected takes with designed pauses at one program level, writes the soundtrack and timeline, and refuses abrupt takes. Captions time cues on the aligned words, never across a thought.

views.title: The picture's gate and render
views.question: What audits the picture before it renders, and what renders it?
views.summary: The picture gate has the Node tool runner run the frame, motion and detail audits and binds the composition, fonts and engine version in its gate record. Picture rendering has the native renderer draw each stage only after a passing record, on a canvas and with no browser.

views.title: Packaging, verification, delivery and review
views.question: How are the films packaged, verified, delivered, reviewed and reproduced?
views.summary: Packaging encodes four films; verification reads each record and decodes each film; delivery sends 25 members and reads them back. Review prompts the independent reviewer; reproduction compares a rebuild with the published release.
